summary: Dashboard CSV export corrupts tracehook token for >30d rows (URL-encoding + truncation)
description:
Issue summary: BrightLoop reports that CSV exports from Dashboard 'Route performance' contain broken trace links for rows older than ~30 days. The exported 'X-Tracehook' header column is URL-encoded incorrectly and often truncated, causing dashboard-to-trace navigation to 404 in our trace service.

Impact: Customer cannot reliably map historical usage rows back to traces for post-incident analysis. Affects dedicated tenant (BrightLoop) and prevents their compliance team from completing audits for the last billing cycle.

Environment: prod (BrightLoop dedicated account), dashboard: Route performance -> Export CSV, region: us-east-1. Affected exports originate from dashboards which include the tracehook token column added via the tracehook header integration.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login as BrightLoop (dedicated) in us-east.
2) Open Console -> Dashboards -> Route performance -> set timeframe to last 90 days.
3) Click 'Export' -> CSV.
4) Open CSV and inspect the tracehook token column (header 'X-Tracehook').
5) For rows older than ~30 days (aligned with retention-compaction boundary) the token contains percent-encoded sequences and appears truncated (example: "trace%0Aabc%3D" or "trace%0D" fragments) and clicking constructed trace link returns 404.

Observed logs / artifacts:
- sample exported CSV attached by customer (BrightLoop_export_2026-02-27.csv) — shows 63/420 rows affected.
- Console export service logs for the customer's export job: job_id=exp-20260227-9923 — stack traces show no exception at export time.
- retention compaction job logs: compaction-window=2026-01-27..2026-02-26 — compression step reports 'filtered header normalization' warnings around 2026-02-26 03:12:11 UTC.

Initial hypothesis: tracehook values are being munged during retention compaction / export rollup step where stored header blobs are compacted and later replayed into CSV exports. The compaction appears to mishandle CRLF and percent-encoding boundaries producing embedded %0A / %0D sequences and truncation.

Workaround suggested to customer: Export narrower time windows that do not include rows crossing the retention-compaction boundary (e.g., last 28 days) OR use the Console API to call the raw /exports endpoint which bypasses the CSV encoder path (temporary).
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Aisha Gupta (customer): We've attached the CSV and timestamped examples. ~15% of the rows point to invalid trace links. This started after last month's retention run — is that related?

2026-03-01 11:05 - Support (Ben Ortega): Thanks Aisha — reproducing locally against a copy of your tenant data. Can you confirm if you rotated any org-wide api keys or changed tracehook config in Feb? We will pull export and compaction logs and escalate to SRE.

2026-03-01 15:30 - SRE (Marta Liu): Reproduced export with test fixture: export of rows spanning retention boundary shows token truncated at first CR (\u000D) and CR is percent-encoded to %0D. Suspect compaction normalization replaced CRLF with literal \n inside stored blob. Captured compaction worker trace: compactor-v2.1 sanitized headers using textwrap library.

2026-03-02 08:22 - Support (Ben Ortega): We're triaging with Platform Eng. Temporary workaround: export in two slices (pre-/post-compaction) or use the internal exports API with param 'raw_headers=true'. Sending steps to Aisha.

2026-03-03 17:40 - Platform Eng (Diego Rivera): Root cause identified: compaction step applied base64->gzip->text processing and then a string replace that attempted to normalize newlines. The replace mistakenly URL-encoded newline bytes when the header blob contained already-percent-encoded segments, resulting in double-encoding and truncation when CSV writer later applied CSV quoting. A patch is ready to stop normalizing bytes and treat header blobs as opaque at compaction time (PR linked).
2026-03-04 10:11 - Aisha Gupta (customer): Confirmed workaround worked for two exports; please advise ETA for permanent fix — compliance deadline next week.
investigation_notes: Reproduced issue in staging fixture by generating headers containing CRLF and percent-encoded payload (\n, %0A). Export path: storage->compaction->export-joiner->csv-emitter. Failure point: compaction normalization stage where 'normalizeNewlines' applied after URL-encoding check.

Binary inspection: header blob pre-compaction contains raw bytes 'trace\r\nabc=...'; post-compaction blob shows 'trace%0D%0Aabc%3D...' then CSV writer truncates at %0D when reconstructing header due to naive substring extraction logic.

Compactor code version: compactor-v2.1 (commit 8a2f4b) used by retention run on 2026-02-26; previous runs used compactor-v2.0 which did not perform the newline normalization and exports were fine. Regression introduced in v2.1.
Customer repro rate: 63/420 rows in provided CSV (15%); affected rows correlate to logs that were compacted in the 2026-02-26 retention window. Newer rows (<30d) unaffected.
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed to prod compactor: revert 'normalizeNewlines' change and mark header blobs as opaque (deployed 2026-03-04 22:38 UTC).
PRs merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/3110 (revert compaction newline normalization), https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7421 (CSV writer robust-quote fix).

Backfill plan: Re-run compaction for affected retention window with patched compactor in dry-run mode to generate corrected blobs, then run a migration job to rewrite export cache for impacted tenant(s). Initial dry-run completed (2026-03-05) — rewrite scheduled 2026-03-07 03:00 UTC for BrightLoop only.
Customer communication: Notified BrightLoop of hotfix and planned one-tenant rewrite. Recommended temporary export-slicing workaround until rewrite completes.
followup_tasks: Schedule migration job to rewrite export cache for all tenants that had compaction run between 2026-02-26 and 2026-02-27.
Add unit tests for compactor to ensure opaque handling of header blobs with percent-encoded content.
Add monitoring alert to detect CSV export trace link 4xx/404 spike (>1% of export rows).
Update runbook: retention-compaction rollback and one-tenant rewrite steps.
